title: DNA Extraction from Biopsy Samples
author: Sonya N. Radvan
materials: Clean work area, supplies, and pipettes with a 10% bleach solution

steps.title: Prepare work area and supplies
steps.instruction: Lay down a fresh paper towel, gather two weigh boats per sample, one scalpel blade per sample, 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes (including one negative and one positive control), a Sharpie, Kimwipes, lab book, a 1 000 µL pipette (cleaned with 10 % bleach), tweezers (minimum three), scalpel handles (minimum three), and a bovine tissue positive control.

steps.title: Set up cleaning beakers
steps.instruction: Prepare three  beakers for decontaminating tweezers and scalpel handles: (1) soap solution (Alconox) mixed with HPLC water, (2) fresh 15 % bleach solution made with HPLC water, (3) clean HPLC water only. After each sample, rinse tools briefly in the soapy beaker, soak in bleach, then rinse well in the clean water before reuse.

steps.title: Calculate and aliquot lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Determine the total volume of lysis buffer needed for all samples plus one positive and one negative control (400 µL per tube). Aliquot the calculated volume into a separate tube, record the calculation in the lab book, label each 1.5 mL tube with the lab code and sample ID, and add 400 µL lysis buffer to each tube.

steps.title: Prepare scale and weigh boat
steps.instruction: Place a new weigh boat on the analytical balance, zero the balance, and have a second clean weigh boat ready for tissue weighing.

steps.title: Record sample metadata
steps.instruction: In the lab book, create a table for the first sample and write down the lab code, sample ID, and any other pertinent information (e.g., DNA ID, mg of tissue, condition).

steps.title: Retrieve and dry tissue
steps.instruction: Using tweezers, pull the tissue out of its storage tube, place it in the weigh boat, close the original tube, and dab the tissue dry with a Kimwipe.

steps.title: Weigh ~40 mg tissue
steps.instruction: Weigh approximately 40 mg of tissue, place the remainder back into the original tube, and try to include skin close to the blubber‑skin interface. Record the exact weight and any quality notes in the lab book.

steps.title: Finely chop tissue
steps.instruction: Using a scalpel, finely chop the weighed tissue into very small pieces to facilitate lysis.

steps.title: Transfer tissue to lysis tube
steps.instruction: Place the chopped tissue pieces into the previously labeled 1.5 mL tube that already contains 400 µL lysis buffer. Double‑check that tube IDs match the sample.

steps.title: Dispose and clean tools
steps.instruction: Discard the weigh boats, Kimwipes, and scalpel blade. Swish the tweezers and scalpel handle in the soapy water, tap to remove excess liquid, then place them in the bleach solution for the next cleaning cycle.

steps.title: Process remaining samples and controls
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 5‑10 for each additional sample. For the positive control, weigh ~40 mg bovine tissue (in DMSO), chop, and add to its tube with lysis buffer. For the negative control, use a tube containing only lysis buffer and treat it identically to the other samples.

steps.title: Lysis incubation
steps.instruction: Let all tubes sit at room temperature in the lysis buffer for 5 days, rotating or mixing them a few times each day.

steps.title: Enter samples into database
steps.instruction: After incubation, add each sample to the MySQL DNA table for the species, obtain a DNA ID, and record the DNA ID in the lab book.

steps.title: Calculate proteinase K aliquot
steps.instruction: Calculate the total volume of proteinase K required (3 spikes of 33.33 µL per tube, including controls), aliquot this volume into a new tube, and record the calculation in the lab book.

steps.title: First proteinase K spike
steps.instruction: Add 33.3 µL proteinase K to each tube, mix well, and incubate at room temperature overnight with occasional mixing.

steps.title: Second proteinase K spike
steps.instruction: Add a second 33.3 µL proteinase K to each tube, mix well, and place the tubes in a 55 °C water bath for 1 hour.

steps.title: Cool to room temperature
steps.instruction: Transfer the tubes to a rack on the bench and let them cool to room temperature for 1 hour.

steps.title: Third proteinase K spike
steps.instruction: Add the third 33.3 µL proteinase K to each tube, mix, and incubate at room temperature overnight with occasional mixing.

steps.title: Prepare phenol:chloroform aliquots
steps.instruction: In the fume hood, aliquot phenol:chloroform into 15 mL or 50 mL Falcon tubes (400 µL per sample, to be added twice). Mix the stock bottle well before aliquoting.

steps.title: First phenol:chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL phenol:chloroform to each sample tube, invert (upend) by hand for 5 minutes, then centrifuge at 12 000 × g for 2 minutes at 4 °C. While centrifuging, prepare a fresh set of tubes containing 400 µL phenol:chloroform. After centrifugation, transfer the clear aqueous layer to the new tubes, invert for 5 minutes, and centrifuge again at 12 000 × g for 2 minutes at 4 °C.

steps.title: Chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: While the samples are in the centrifuge, aliquot 400 µL chloroform into another set of 1.5 mL tubes. After the phenol:chloroform spin, transfer the aqueous layer to the chloroform tubes, invert for 5 minutes, and centrifuge at 12 000 × g for 2 minutes at 4 °C.

steps.title: Activate MicroCon membrane
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL TE buffer to each MicroCon column to activate the membrane.

steps.title: Load aqueous layer onto column
steps.instruction: Transfer the aqueous layer obtained from the chloroform extraction into the corresponding MicroCon column.

steps.title: First DNA binding spin
steps.instruction: Spin the column at 1500 × g for 15 minutes at 4 °C. Discard the flow‑through into a waste beaker.

steps.title: First TE wash
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL TE to the upper reservoir of the column, then spin again at 1500 × g for 15 minutes at 4 °C. Discard the effluent.

steps.title: Second TE wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the addition of 200 µL TE and spin at 1500 × g for 15 minutes at 4 °C, discarding the effluent.

steps.title: Third TE wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the addition of 200 µL TE and spin at 1500 × g for 15 minutes at 4 °C, discarding the effluent.

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Add the desired elution volume of TE (30–100 µL) to the column membrane, place the column upside‑down into a new labeled collection tube (containing the DNA ID), and spin at 2500 × g for 3 minutes at 4 °C to collect the DNA.

steps.title: Quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Aliquot 2 µL of the eluted DNA into a Qubit assay tube for immediate quantification to minimize freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Store DNA
steps.instruction: Store the remaining DNA at –20 °C.

steps.title: Record final information
steps.instruction: Enter all relevant data (tube label, lab code, DNA ID, mg tissue used, comments, storage location) into the lab book and update the DNA table in the database with the storage location.

steps.title: Prepare fume hood
steps.instruction: Lay fresh paper towels in the fume hood and ensure all reagents and labelled 1.5 mL tubes are present. MicroCon columns and collection tubes need not be placed inside the hood.

steps.title: Final aqueous transfer note
steps.instruction: If the aqueous layer exceeds 400 µL (MicroCon capacity ≈450 µL), repeat the transfer and spin steps (steps 39‑41) until the entire volume has passed through the column.
